newsitem.title: USA: New jobless claims up in latest week.
newsitem.headline: New jobless claims up in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans claiming first-time jobless benefits rose last week, the government said Thursday.

The Labour Department said claims in the week ended Jan. 25 advanced to 351,000 from a revised 341,000 in the week earlier. Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 348,000 in the January 25 week.
The more closely watched four-week moving average, which helps to smooth out weekly fluctuations in the data, fell to 344,750 from a revised 350,250.
Total benefit rolls remained unchanged at about 2.45 million in the week ended Jan. 18, the latest period for which that data were available.
The department said 29 states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Jan. 18.
Among the largest were North Carolina with 19,383; Tennessee with 13,611; South Carolina with 10,262; and Alabama with 8,233.
North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the construction, tobacco, textile, apparel, furniture, lumber, rubber and non-electrical machinery industries.
Tennessee had fewer layoffs in a variety of industries.
South Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the food industry, while Alabama had fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel, furniture and lumber industries.
Labour said no states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Jan. 18 week.
